title: Tuition Panic Budget Ladder
oneLiner: A parent decision console that shows how much private education spending is actually buying score confidence versus household strain before the family silently overcommits.
targetUser: Parents of elementary to high school students who are paying for academies, tutors, or test prep and feel mounting anxiety about whether the spend is still rational.
keyUX: Compare current education spending against household runway, expected outcome confidence, and child overload signals, then choose a saner next-month plan.
stitchPrompt: Design a desktop family decision console called Tuition Panic Budget Ladder for parents paying for academies, tutors, and test prep under rising anxiety. It should help them see how much private education spending is actually buying score confidence versus household strain, child overload, and financial fragility. Include an education spend pressure summary, a subject-by-subject ROI ladder, a family cashflow strain panel, a student overload signal tracker, a next-month cut-or-keep simulator, and a parent decision memo drawer. Design direction: use a financial-analyst aesthetic with disciplined navy structure, warm paper-like surfaces, sharp comparison hierarchy, and restrained alert accents so the product feels protective, rational, and emotionally grounded under family pressure.
